title: Virginia's 9th Congressional District election, 2026
description: Virginia's 9th Congressional District covers most of rural Southwest Virginia, including the New River Valley and the Virginia side of the Tri-Cities area. This is a safely Republican district (Cook PVI R+22) where incumbent Republican Rep. Morgan Griffith, first elected in 2010, is seeking re-election. Three Democrats — Douglas Crockett, Adam Murphy, and Joy Powers — are competing in the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary to challenge Griffith, while Michael Jackson is running as an independent. The district's political dynamics center on economic concerns such as the cost of living, healthcare access, and rural infrastructure, with the candidates offering contrasting visions on how to address these issues.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 Virginia's 9th Congressional District general election as of the research date.

candidates.name: H. Morgan Griffith
candidates.summary: Morgan Griffith is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Virginia's 9th Congressional District, first elected in 2010 and re-elected with 72.5% of the vote in 2024. He previously served as Majority Leader of the Virginia House of Delegates from 2000 to 2010. Griffith is a member of the House Freedom Caucus and serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee.

candidates.name: Douglas Crockett
candidates.summary: Douglas Crockett is a retired United Methodist pastor and attorney running for the Democratic nomination in Virginia's 9th Congressional District. A native of Wythe County, he is a graduate of Emory & Henry College and William & Mary Law School, and served churches across Virginia for more than 30 years while also practicing law. This is his first run for public office.

candidates.name: Adam Murphy
candidates.summary: Adam Murphy is a progressive Democratic candidate running for the nomination in Virginia's 9th Congressional District. A software developer and first-time candidate, Murphy earned a B.S. in Software Development from Western Governors University in 2017. His campaign focuses on lowering the cost of living, Medicare for all, rebuilding Southwest Virginia's manufacturing base, and supporting small businesses and farms.

candidates.name: Joy Powers
candidates.summary: Joy Powers is a fourth-generation cattle farmer, small business owner, and Bedford County mother running for the Democratic nomination in Virginia's 9th Congressional District. She previously ran as the Democratic nominee for Virginia's 51st House of Delegates district in 2025. Her campaign focuses on affordability, rural healthcare, public education, and protecting Virginia's farmland and rural way of life.

candidates.summary: Michael Jackson is an independent candidate running for U.S. House in Virginia's 9th Congressional District. His campaign emphasizes accessibility, with a pledge to hold monthly mobile offices in the district, and focuses on lowering costs, workforce development, and infrastructure improvements. Ballotpedia lists him as a general election candidate.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling is available for this race, so confidence is constrained to medium. However, the structural factors are decisive: Virginia's 9th District has a Cook PVI of R+22 (safely Republican), and incumbent Rep. Morgan Griffith has held the seat since 2010, winning 72.5% in his most recent re-election. Democrats have a contested three-way primary (August 4, 2026) with no nominee yet, and all three Democratic candidates are first-time federal office seekers with limited name recognition. Independent Michael Jackson is running but has no demonstrated districtwide strength. Given the district's deep Republican baseline, the incumbent's long tenure and strong electoral track record, and a fractured opposition still selecting a nominee, this remains a Safe Republican race.
